partial: AC-07.2.1 says at least one child block must be filled in and that every child question is required whenever asked, but no cited fact or decision backs either.

After an HR change, 'incomplete - HR must complete' is specified for the tariff code and for 'subject to source tax'. What happens to the pension fund results when an HR change makes an answer apply that was never asked? Two examples: a move from abroad to Switzerland, where the canton was never asked; and a change from Single to Married, where the spouse's date of birth was never asked. Should the canton for the fund, and the fund registration with civil status Married, also show 'incomplete - HR must complete'? Or should the canton keep showing Zurich until HR enters it? Which derived results does the 'incomplete' state apply to?

AC-06.6.5's first example still has a second, output-side 'Denomination' column expecting 'required' after an HR change, while D-053 says examples after an HR change expect 'HR must complete', not that the question is asked/required. The second example (civil status changed to Married) does not show the never-asked 'Spouse gainfully employed' answer at all. What exactly should these examples expect, so the 'incomplete' acceptance test checks the right thing?

The 'Full source tax tariff code' rule (rows 3-4, D-052) gives 'incomplete - HR must complete' only when the tariff letter or church-tax suffix cannot be determined; the child digit is 'any'. What is the result when HR adds a child (e.g. 'Has children' changed to yes or a new child block) whose per-child questions were never answered, so the child digit cannot be determined? Should that also be 'incomplete - HR must complete'?

After an HR change, 'Subject to source tax' itself may be undeterminable (e.g. HR changes the address from abroad to Switzerland and nationality/C permit were never asked; or to Liechtenstein and daily return was never asked). The tariff code rule only covers subject yes/no and Liechtenstein yes/no. Should the tariff code (and the subject-to-source-tax result) show 'incomplete - HR must complete' in these cases?
"(The internal expression evaluates one child block; it is summed over all blocks.)" - Refers to an internal formula ('internal expression') rather than business language. D-045 forbids this.

"free text is not accepted and the country is required" - Prescribes how the input field behaves (no free text). Choosing from the list is already the business rule; how input is restricted is up to engineering.
"(The internal expression evaluates one child block; it is summed over all blocks.)" - Refers to an internal formula ('internal expression') rather than business language. D-045 forbids this.

info.message: The first working day 'must lie within one year after the questionnaire is sent'. Can it also be before the send date or in the past, for example when the employee has already started or fills in the questionnaire late? Sending the questionnaire is part of the later HR-side spec, so which date counts as 'sent' for this check? Is there also any plausibility check on the spouse's date of birth?

The stories disagree on when a missing required answer blocks the employee. US-02.1 says the employee 'cannot leave step 1 complete' without the name or date of birth. US-02.2 says the address 'step cannot be completed'. US-03.1, US-04.1 and AC-01.8.2 say the employee only cannot submit. Should a missing required answer stop the employee from moving to the next step, or only from submitting (so a partly filled step can be saved and left, as US-01.7 allows)? And if the employee can go on, how is a step that is not complete shown?

The calculator asks whether the certificate of residence has been provided ('beigebracht'). The story asks whether the employee 'has a certificate of residence for HR'. Does 'yes' mean the certificate has already been given to HR, or only that the employee has one? Should HR expect a certificate later for 'no' as well as for 'not yet', or only for 'not yet'?

Expected results for the same question still differ between stories. AC-01.2.2 marks the canton as 'asked', but US-02.4 marks it 'required'. AC-01.2.4 marks the spouse's date of birth and the spouse's nationality as 'asked', but US-04.2 and US-05.2 mark them 'required'. US-06.3 has 'required' for a married employee and 'asked' for a registered partner. Several rows also show '–' for questions that always apply, for example First name for the Germany resident in AC-01.2.2. Is there a real difference between 'asked' and 'required' (can any of these answers be left empty?), and does '–' mean 'not checked in this example'?

Several example tables use the same item as both an input and an expected result, with values that do not match. In AC-01.1.1, Nationality is '–' as an input but 'not asked' as a result for Stefan. In AC-01.1.2, 'More than 45 non-return days' is 'yes' or 'no' as an input but '–' or 'not asked' as a result. The same happens in US-07.3 and US-07.5. Which of the two values is the expected outcome a tester should check?

In the AC-04.4.1 example table, the spouse's date of birth is '–' for Married, but 'required' for Registered partnership and Separated. It is also '–' for Single, but 'not asked' for Divorced and Widowed. Should Married expect 'required' and Single expect 'not asked', as US-04.2 says?

AC-07.2.1 says 'At least one child block is filled in' when the employee answered 'yes' to having children. The trace check notes that no cited source backs this. Is it a confirmed rule, and if so what happens when the employee removes the last child block? Is that blocked, or is 'has children' then treated as 'no'?

The 'Tariff letter' rule keeps row 6 (G -> Q, citing D-051) while D-006 drops the tariff G/Q cases and the base letter rule says G cannot occur. Should the G -> Q mapping be built and tested at all, or removed?

uncited_units.text: HR meeting transcript Everyone and everything here is fictional. Anna is the HR manager at Muster AG. Leo works in product at Lonio.
Can you hear me okay? You're a bit quiet.
Is this better? I'm in the small meeting room, the big one is taken. Sorry, let me just close the door.
Much better. So, thanks for making the time. The idea today is simple. We want your new employees to give us everything once, so that you stop chasing them for
Yes, please. Right now it's a mess. I have a Word document, then an Excel file, and then I type everything into the portals by hand. Last month I spent a full a
Okay. And how many people do you hire in a year?
Around twenty. More in summer. We're about a hundred and fifty people now, mostly here in Zurich.
Good. Let's start with the biggest pain. What takes you the most time?
Okay, that's clear. And the questionnaire itself is what?
Great. Do you also want a photo? Some customers ask for one.
It could. Do you want that from day one?
We're with Pensionskasse Muster. They have a portal, it's quite old. I'll send you some screenshots of it after this call, that's easier than me explaining it.
Perfect. What do you need for the fund that you don't have?
Sorry, one second, someone's at my door. [pause] Okay, I'm back, sorry. Where were we?
The Julia story. It doesn't matter.
Right. What else about the employee affects the fund? Are they married, things like that?
And what are the options in that list?
Okay. Noted. Can I go back to source tax? You said all non-Swiss employees.
Sure, send it if it's easy. Do people need anything from you on the first day? Laptops, things like that? I just want to see if that belongs in the same form.
Okay. Anything else on who needs to do it? I'd rather hear all of it now.
Only the timing. When can we have this?
I'll come back to you on that this week, once we've gone through your screenshots.
Good. I'll send them after lunch. Thanks, Leo.

open_questions.question: Does Lonio's computed tariff code match the Zurich calculator for the unexplored paths: the residence block for tariffs A/B/H, the inferred per-child rows, more than 3 children, and the H3N/P3N examples?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Lonio now owns the tariff result instead of HR clicking through the calculator; unverified paths could produce wrong source tax codes.
options: Domain expert compares computed codes with the calculator for the listed paths before go-live
Go live and fall back to HR's manual check for unexplored paths
open_questions.recommendation: Domain expert check before go-live (D-009); observed rows win over derived ones (D-046).

questions.question: The first working day 'must lie within one year after the questionnaire is sent'. Can it also be before the send date or in the past, for example when the employee has already started or fills in the questionnaire late? Sending the questionnaire is part of the later HR-side spec, so which date counts as 'sent' for this check? Is there also any plausibility check on the spouse's date of birth?

The stories disagree on when a missing required answer blocks the employee. US-02.1 says the employee 'cannot leave step 1 complete' without the name or date of birth. US-02.2 says the address 'step cannot be completed'. US-03.1, US-04.1 and AC-01.8.2 say the employee only cannot submit. Should a missing required answer stop the employee from moving to the next step, or only from submitting (so a partly filled step can be saved and left, as US-01.7 allows)? And if the employee can go on, how is a step that is not complete shown?

The calculator asks whether the certificate of residence has been provided ('beigebracht'). The story asks whether the employee 'has a certificate of residence for HR'. Does 'yes' mean the certificate has already been given to HR, or only that the employee has one? Should HR expect a certificate later for 'no' as well as for 'not yet', or only for 'not yet'?

Expected results for the same question still differ between stories. AC-01.2.2 marks the canton as 'asked', but US-02.4 marks it 'required'. AC-01.2.4 marks the spouse's date of birth and the spouse's nationality as 'asked', but US-04.2 and US-05.2 mark them 'required'. US-06.3 has 'required' for a married employee and 'asked' for a registered partner. Several rows also show '–' for questions that always apply, for example First name for the Germany resident in AC-01.2.2. Is there a real difference between 'asked' and 'required' (can any of these answers be left empty?), and does '–' mean 'not checked in this example'?

After an HR change, 'incomplete - HR must complete' is specified for the tariff code and for 'subject to source tax'. What happens to the pension fund results when an HR change makes an answer apply that was never asked? Two examples: a move from abroad to Switzerland, where the canton was never asked; and a change from Single to Married, where the spouse's date of birth was never asked. Should the canton for the fund, and the fund registration with civil status Married, also show 'incomplete - HR must complete'? Or should the canton keep showing Zurich until HR enters it? Which derived results does the 'incomplete' state apply to?

Several example tables use the same item as both an input and an expected result, with values that do not match. In AC-01.1.1, Nationality is '–' as an input but 'not asked' as a result for Stefan. In AC-01.1.2, 'More than 45 non-return days' is 'yes' or 'no' as an input but '–' or 'not asked' as a result. The same happens in US-07.3 and US-07.5. Which of the two values is the expected outcome a tester should check?

In the AC-04.4.1 example table, the spouse's date of birth is '–' for Married, but 'required' for Registered partnership and Separated. It is also '–' for Single, but 'not asked' for Divorced and Widowed. Should Married expect 'required' and Single expect 'not asked', as US-04.2 says?

AC-07.2.1 says 'At least one child block is filled in' when the employee answered 'yes' to having children. The trace check notes that no cited source backs this. Is it a confirmed rule, and if so what happens when the employee removes the last child block? Is that blocked, or is 'has children' then treated as 'no'?

AC-06.6.5's first example still has a second, output-side 'Denomination' column expecting 'required' after an HR change, while D-053 says examples after an HR change expect 'HR must complete', not that the question is asked/required. The second example (civil status changed to Married) does not show the never-asked 'Spouse gainfully employed' answer at all. What exactly should these examples expect, so the 'incomplete' acceptance test checks the right thing?

The 'Full source tax tariff code' rule (rows 3-4, D-052) gives 'incomplete - HR must complete' only when the tariff letter or church-tax suffix cannot be determined; the child digit is 'any'. What is the result when HR adds a child (e.g. 'Has children' changed to yes or a new child block) whose per-child questions were never answered, so the child digit cannot be determined? Should that also be 'incomplete - HR must complete'?

After an HR change, 'Subject to source tax' itself may be undeterminable (e.g. HR changes the address from abroad to Switzerland and nationality/C permit were never asked; or to Liechtenstein and daily return was never asked). The tariff code rule only covers subject yes/no and Liechtenstein yes/no. Should the tariff code (and the subject-to-source-tax result) show 'incomplete - HR must complete' in these cases?

The 'Tariff letter' rule keeps row 6 (G -> Q, citing D-051) while D-006 drops the tariff G/Q cases and the base letter rule says G cannot occur. Should the G -> Q mapping be built and tested at all, or removed?

review.summary: All 300+ examples pass and there are no errors or blocking open questions. The only open question, OQ-calculator-coverage, is non-blocking. Nothing from the previous review is fully resolved. The biggest gap is the 'incomplete - HR must complete' state after an HR change. Its scope is still undefined, and three major dev-refinement questions remain. The tariff_code trace warning still shows the old child-digit expression. Engineering can start on the main flow, but PO decisions are needed on the incomplete state, the tariff_code expression and the tech leaks.

findings.title: Scope of the 'incomplete - HR must complete' state is undefined
findings.why: D-052 and D-053 cover the tariff letter and church-tax suffix only. The following are not covered: pension fund canton, fund civil status Married without a spouse date of birth, an undeterminable child digit, and an undeterminable 'subject to source tax' after an HR change. Engineering would have to guess.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement US-01.6 (major); feature.md x2 (major); D-052, D-053
findings.action: Add a decision listing every derived result that can show 'incomplete'. Cover canton, spouse date of birth, child digit and subject-to-source-tax, and state what each shows when its inputs were never asked.

findings.title: AC-06.6.5 examples: expectations after an HR change are ambiguous
findings.why: The examples now pass, but the first still expects Denomination 'required', which contradicts D-053. The second omits the never-asked spouse-employment answer. The test may assert the wrong thing.
findings.action: Rewrite both examples to expect 'HR must complete' for the unasked answers. Show the spouse-employment input in the second example.

findings.title: tariff_code expression vs child-digit statement
findings.why: The trace judge still reports if_else(child_count,1,0), which only gives 0 or 1. D-052 requires the number of counted children (for example C3Y). Codes for two or more children would be wrong. The report may predate the D-052 override.
findings.action: Confirm the expression after D-052 yields the child count, and add an example with 2 or more children.

findings.title: Technical wording leaks into the spec
findings.why: D-045 forbids internal-formula language. 'ISO 3166' is implementation vocabulary, and 'free text is not accepted' dictates how the input behaves.
findings.evidence: tech_leak: feature.md and information.md ('internal expression'); US-02.3; item.address_country, nationality, spouse_nationality; AC-02.3.1, AC-05.1.2, AC-05.2.3
findings.action: Replace these with business wording: 'chosen from a list of countries, plus stateless'. Drop the 'internal expression' sentence and the free-text sentence.

findings.title: Rules rely on facts and gating that no cited source backs
findings.why: The following are unbacked or cited incorrectly: Liechtenstein/non_return_days_45 gating, tariff purposes, 'G→Q cannot occur', and rows citing facts missing from the rule's citation list. This weakens traceability.
findings.evidence: trace_judge: questionnaire_flow, base_tariff_letter, cross_border_tariff, tariff_letter, calculator_residence, pension_fund_canton, liechtenstein_no_source_tax, has_children, child_*, spouse_gainful_employment; D-002, D-047 not cited
findings.action: Add the missing citations (D-002, D-047, the cited calculator facts). Mark the remaining rows as inferred decisions.

findings.title: G→Q mapping kept although D-006 drops G/Q
findings.why: Row 6 of the tariff letter rule (D-051) conflicts with D-006 and with the base letter rule. This risks dead code and unneeded tests.
findings.action: Decide whether to remove the G→Q row or keep it with a stated reason.

findings.title: Unconfirmed rule: at least one child block required
findings.why: AC-07.2.1 requires at least one child block and every child question to be required. No source backs either. What happens when the last block is removed is undefined.
findings.action: Confirm the rule with HR. Define what happens when the last block is removed (blocked, or 'has children' becomes no).

findings.title: Inconsistent expected values across example tables
findings.why: 'asked' and 'required' are used for the same question. '–' is used as both input and result with mismatched values. Spouse date of birth expectations differ between Married/Single and Divorced/Widowed.
findings.action: Define the vocabulary: asked vs required, and what '–' means. Normalise the tables.

findings.title: Conflicting rules on when a missing answer blocks the employee
findings.why: Some stories block leaving the step and others block only submission. US-01.7 allows saving a partly filled step.
findings.action: Decide: block submission only (recommended), and align the stories.

findings.title: Calculator coverage unverified; minor semantics open
findings.why: The unexplored tariff paths (A/B/H residence block, inferred per-child rows, more than 3 children, H3N/P3N) could give wrong codes. Several calculator facts are only partly verified. Also open: certificate 'provided' vs 'has', the 'sent' date for the start-date check, and the insurance start-date error behaviour (F-pension_portal-e45e5b unused).
findings.evidence: OQ-calculator-coverage (non-blocking); fact_judge F-zh_source_tax_calculator-037b1c, 64ac33, dc0ae9, c8aa5e, 2754e8; dev_refinement US-08.2, US-03.1; coverage
